opex.name: Operating expenses
opex.note: Research, engineering and running the fabs' business side — TSMC reports this as one line in its earnings release.

follow100Note: For every $100 TSMC took in, $55.62 survived as profit — the fattest margin of any company on this site. Advanced chips (7-nanometer and below) were 77% of wafer revenue. Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.
footerNote: TSMC reports in New Taiwan dollars (revenue NT$1,270.4B; net income NT$706.6B). Dollar figures are converted at the quarter's average rate of NT$31.60 per US$1 — the rate TSMC itself reports; its stated US-dollar revenue was $40.20B. Operating expenses are shown as one line, net of about NT$5.3B of other operating income, because the earnings release does not split them out. The tax line is set so the flow lands on net income attributable to TSMC shareholders.
oneTimers: Non-operating income jumped to NT$95.8B from NT$28.8B in Q1, helped by TSMC's sale of an 8.1% stake in Vanguard International Semiconductor in May 2026 — a one-off that flatters the profit growth rate.
otherDetail: Non-operating items of NT$95.8B (about $3.0B) — interest, investment gains and other income outside the fabs, including a gain on selling an 8.1% stake in Vanguard International Semiconductor in May.

segments.note: Chips for AI data centers and servers — now two-thirds of everything TSMC sells.

segments.name: Smartphone

takeaways.text: High-performance computing — AI accelerators and server chips — reached 66% of revenue, up 20% in a single quarter. Smartphone chips fell 4% ahead of autumn phone launches.
takeaways.title: AI chips are the business now

takeaways.text: Gross margin hit 67.7%, up from 58.6% a year ago, as premium 3nm and 5nm wafers made up 63% of wafer revenue. The new 2nm node shipped its first revenue — 3% of wafers.
takeaways.title: Margins keep climbing

takeaways.text: Net income rose 77% to NT$706.6B on 36% revenue growth (in NT$) — operating leverage, plus a jump in non-operating income helped by the Vanguard stake sale.
takeaways.title: Profit rose much faster than sales

verdict: TSMC's revenue rose 34% to $40.2B as AI chips reached two-thirds of sales — and with a 67.7% gross margin, it kept $22.4B as profit, up 77% in a year.
